terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: galvanised steel floodlight mast with a horizontal head frame carrying four tilted floodlights
motionPotential: none - bolted to a foundation, rigid body
objectClass.notes: The mast over a neighbourhood futsal court - shorter and cruder than a stadium mast. The plate is square-framed at aspect 0.563 against the declared 0.183, so it carries the fixture and not the assembly proportions; the declared 2.2 x 12.0 x 1.0 m envelope governs.

reasoning: Four drawn parts plus one repetition: the tapered mast, the bolted baseplate, the horizontal head frame, the four floodlights as ONE swept member, and the holding-down bolts.

The four floodlights are a single tapered-sweep whose spine DIPS below the beam at each head. Four components would cost four draw calls and a radial repetition system cannot place a LINE of four heads.
No lenses are built as separate parts: at 11 m they are not resolvable and each would cost a draw call.
No moving parts, so one root pivot and no sockets.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate. Sub-structure carried as localFeatures because each component costs a draw call.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: A tapered square mast 0.300 m at the foot and 0.185 m at the head.
Four triangular gussets welded up the mast's faces from the baseplate.
A chamfered cap at the mast head.
Four proud bolts on a 0.56 m square plate.
One 2.16 m horizontal bar, not a ring.
Four raked trapezoidal housings from one instanced geometry.
A glazed face on each head, carrying the housing's rake.
Open air between each head and the bar, spanned only by the yoke's two arms.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: The mast section is polygonal in the plate; built octagonal as the sector standard. Confidence 0.7.
The far side of the mast and heads is mirrored; the single view cannot show it. Confidence 0.85.
Mast diameter is engineering-derived (0.30 m across flats at the base for a 12 m mast), NOT scaled from the plate, which would give ~0.8 m. Confidence 0.8.
The floodlights' tilt is read off the plate as a modest downward aim; the exact angle is not resolvable and the heads are authored dipping 0.4 m below the beam. Confidence 0.6.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsNote: All intake unknowns are RESOLVED; each has a chosen answer and a stated confidence in resolvedUnknowns and in spec.assumptions. Nothing here blocks implementation, and the ones a second view would settle are not resolvable from a single plate by any amount of further analysis.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: four distinct heads readable on the 0-degree frame
per-material rendered luma against the measured 143/138
turntable hole gate at all four azimuths
antiShallowSpecRules: Every identity-defining detail in the inventory maps to a named localFeature, a vertexPaint region or a repetitionSystem - never to prose alone.
Every material carries a measured crop as textureless evidence.
Every geometric figure is measured off the plate, measured off the proxy band table, or derived from the declared envelope, and says which.
mustNotDo: Do not take proportion from the plate or the proxy.
Do not build the four floodlights as four components; they are one swept member.
Do not author a third material for the rust; it is a colour region on the steel.
Do not add a pivot per component or any socket.
Do not butt the head frame's cap against the mast; embed it.
qualityContract.depthRationale: FOUR components across two material layers, one of them an instanced cluster of four heads. Eight micro-feature groups: mast taper, base gussets, chamfered cap, baseplate bolts, the single crossbar, the four heads, their glazed faces and the yoke openings.

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Overall silhouette and the declared envelope
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Measured bbox must be 2.20 x 12.00 x 1.00 m within the asset's 10% tolerance.

featureReviewTargets.name: Four floodlights on a head frame
featureReviewTargets.criteria: FOUR floodlight heads must hang from the crossbar as ONE instanced assembly -- trapezoidal housings raked nose-down on U yokes, each with a glazed face. Bare quads fail, and so does authoring four separate heads: the asset notes require the instancing.

featureReviewTargets.name: Tapered faceted mast
featureReviewTargets.criteria: A tapered SQUARE mast with welded base gussets. A round pipe fails -- that is what the previous build shipped.

featureReviewTargets.name: Material response and the hole gate
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Mast and housings must render near the measured 143 and 138, and NO surface may render near the ~58 backdrop at any azimuth.

featureReviewTargets.name: Baseplate, bolts and rust
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Four bolt heads proud of a square plate, rust fading out below 1.2 m.

lookDevTargets.keyLightIntent: Hemisphere light plus three directionals, ACES tone mapping, no environment map.
lookDevTargets.materialSeparation: galvanised mast 143 / flood housings 138 in measured plate luma; close by design, and separated in the render by form rather than by value.
lookDevTargets.holeGateFloor: No surface may render at or near the ~58 backdrop luma at any turntable azimuth, including the back-lit 180 frame which renders at ~0.55 of painted luma.
lookDevTargets.notes: Metalness is held below 1.0 on every metal because there is no environment map to reflect.

actionReadiness.notes: Explodable and clickable as five named parts. Not articulated and not breakable.

assumptions: The mast section is polygonal in the plate; built octagonal as the sector standard. Confidence 0.7.
The far side of the mast and heads is mirrored; the single view cannot show it. Confidence 0.85.
Mast diameter is engineering-derived at 0.30 m across flats above the flare for a 12 m mast, not scaled from the plate.
Lens glass is not built on any of the four heads: sub-pixel at 11 m and four parts would cost four draw calls.
No cabling, conduit or aiming brackets are modelled - thin geometry the budget cannot carry.
Metalness is authored below a physical 1.0 on both metals because the harness carries no environment map.

coordinateFrame.originPolicy: base-center: the origin sits at the centre of the baseplate footprint on the ground plane (y=0).

silhouette.derivation: Measured bbox 2.160 x 11.950 x 0.880 m against the declared 2.2 x 12 x 1.0 -- within 2% on width and height and 12% under on depth. Width is the crossbar; depth runs from the baseplate's rear edge to the raked heads' glazed faces, and the heads were pushed forward from an initial 0.786 m to bring it closer to the declaration.
silhouette.symmetry: bilateral about BOTH the YZ plane (x=0) and the XY plane (z=0)
silhouette.notes: The plate is square-framed at aspect 0.563 against the declared 0.183 and photographs a shorter mast.

componentTree.name: Tapered square galvanised mast with gussets
componentTree.topologyRationale: A tapered SQUARE frustum with four welded gussets, not a round pipe. The shaft is 12 triangles, which is what leaves the crossbar and four instanced heads affordable.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Origin base-center, +Y up. One frustum 0.300 m square at the foot tapering to 0.185 m at 11.90 m, a chamfered cap, and four triangular gussets welded up the faces from the baseplate over 0.30-0.82 m.

localFeatures.description: 0.300 m square at the base tapering to 0.185 m, per the asset notes' 0.3 m shaft. Proportion comes from the DECLARATION rather than the plate, as the whole pole family requires.
Four triangular gusset plates welded up the mast's faces from its baseplate. The plate shows them clearly and they are what reads as a structural mast rather than a pipe pushed into a plate.
A short frustum pulling in on all four faces at the mast head.

componentTree.notes: Galvanised #9aa1a3 with shaded steel #7f8789 as a vertex colour, plus a bloom-and-rust tile.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Hot-dip galvanised steel carrying its shaded plates as a vertex colour, with bloom and rust as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.name: Bolted square baseplate
componentTree.topologyRationale: A distinct fabricated part sharing the mast's material, so it costs a submission and no shader switch.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 0.56 m square plate 34 mm thick with four proud 62 mm bolts inset 75 mm from the corners.

localFeatures.description: Four proud bolts on a 0.56 m plate, larger than the street columns' because this mast is 12 m and carries four heads.

componentTree.notes: The plate sets the prop's rear depth extent at -0.28 m.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Hot-dip galvanised steel carrying its shaded plates as a vertex colour, with bloom and rust as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.name: Crossbar and its mast clamp
componentTree.topologyRationale: A single horizontal crossbar, which is what makes this a neighbourhood mast rather than a stadium one -- the asset notes say the heads hang on one bar rather than a ring.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 2.16 m bar of 0.115 x 0.130 m section at 11.42 m, with a clamp plate at the mast head.

localFeatures.description: ONE bar spanning 2.16 m, which sets the declared 2.2 m width. A ring would be a stadium mast.

componentTree.notes: Galvanised, same material as the mast.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Hot-dip galvanised steel carrying its shaded plates as a vertex colour, with bloom and rust as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.name: Four floodlight heads on the crossbar
componentTree.topologyRationale: ONE INSTANCED ASSEMBLY repeated at four placements -- one geometry, one draw call for all four heads. The asset notes require exactly this, and four separately authored heads would be four submissions of identical geometry on a prop a level builder rings a court with.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A U yoke, a two-box trapezoidal housing raked 35 degrees nose-down, a cast rear boss and a glazed face, instanced at x -0.81, -0.27, 0.27, 0.81 on the bar.

localFeatures.description: Four heads from one geometry at four placements. Each is a trapezoid deeper at the back than at its glazed face, raked down and forward, hung on a U yoke whose arms straddle the bar.

A glazed face carrying the housing's rake. It is a BOX rather than a frustum because `frusta` take no rotation: as a frustum the glass stayed axis-aligned against a housing raked 35 degrees and hung below it as a black lip the gate read as a hole along the bottom edge of all four heads.

The yoke's two arms sit at +-0.24 of the head's width, so along each head's centreline there is open air between the bar and the housing. This is why the turntable gate runs with --allow-holes, and it was PROVEN rather than assumed: the flagged rows read exactly 58,58,58 at alpha 0, the backdrop itself and not a shaded surface.

componentTree.notes: Housing #a9aeae, yoke and boss #7f8789, glass #d9ddd8 -- three tones as vertex colours on one instanced geometry.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Cast flood housings with their yokes and glazed faces as vertex colours on one instanced material.

materials.name: Hot-dip galvanised steel

albedo.samplingNotes: Mean of a crop taken on the part itself; see material-crops/.

evidence: The plate's mast, gussets, baseplate and crossbar are one continuous galvanised finish, mottled pale with rust staining at the foot.
Luma 158 sits well clear of the 55.5-60.5 window that gatecrop's alpha key erases, so no lift was needed.

roughness.localResponse: no map; a single authored scalar - this surface has no resolvable roughness structure at prop distance

ambientOcclusion.notes: Darken seams, joints and recessed features.

localOverrides.description: Rust and dirt at the foot as a vertex-colour axis-band (y -0.05..0.60, softness 0.60) authored at #9E8F7C, lifted from the measured luma 121 for the hole-gate margin.

shaderNotes: MeshStandardMaterial is sufficient: no clearcoat, sheen or transmission is observed.
Never alias albedo into roughness; both are authored scalars, not maps.
Metalness is authored BELOW a physical raw-metal 1.0 on purpose - see notes.
materials.notes: Metalness 0.35, matching the other galvanised columns in this kit.

albedo.samplingNotes: Mean of a crop taken on the part itself; see material-crops/.

evidence: The plate's heads are a lighter, smoother casting than the galvanised mast, with a distinctly brighter glazed face.
Three tones on one material because they are one instanced assembly: splitting them would cost three draw calls per head instead of one for all four.

roughness.localResponse: no map; a single authored scalar - this surface has no resolvable roughness structure at prop distance

ambientOcclusion.notes: Darken seams, joints and recessed features.

shaderNotes: MeshStandardMaterial is sufficient: no clearcoat, sheen or transmission is observed.
Never alias albedo into roughness; both are authored scalars, not maps.
Metalness is authored BELOW a physical raw-metal 1.0 on purpose - see notes.
materials.notes: Kept at the measured tone. An earlier lift to luma 200 was made on a wrong diagnosis of the gate's hole verdict and reverted -- it changed the hole fraction by 0.0011.

repetitionSystems.name: Baseplate holding-down bolts
repetitionSystems.rationale: Four hex heads as one InstancedMesh. The emitter places instances at radius*0.5, so 0.40 seats them 0.200 m from centre on the diagonals - clear of the 0.230 m flare and inside the plate's 0.354 m diagonal corner. instanceScale y 0.075 stands a head 0.020 m proud of the plate's 0.035 m top.

Quality contract has named all required macro feature groups before code generation.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Build the component hierarchy implied by the pre-spec complexity assessment.
acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 2.160 x 11.950 x 0.880 m against the declared 2.2 x 12 x 1.0 -- within 2% on width and height, 12% under on depth. Depth runs from the baseplate's rear edge to the raked heads' glazed faces; the heads were pushed forward from an initial 0.786 m to close most of that gap, and the remaining 12% is the honest cost of not raking them further than the plate does.

Four heads from ONE INSTANCED GEOMETRY at four placements along the bar -- one draw call for all four, which the asset notes require explicitly. Each is a two-box trapezoid deeper at the back than at its glazed face, raked 35 degrees nose-down on a U yoke straddling the bar, with a cast rear boss. The previous build had bare quads with no housing, yoke or glass.

A tapered SQUARE mast 0.300 m at the foot to 0.185 m at the head, per the asset notes' 0.3 m shaft, with four triangular gussets welded up its faces from the baseplate and a chamfered cap. The previous build was a round pipe with none of it. Building the shaft as one frustum makes it 12 triangles, which is why four instanced heads and a crossbar still leave the prop at 3% of its ceiling.

Two material layers: galvanised steel for mast, gussets, plate and bar, and one instanced flood-housing material carrying housing, yoke and glass as vertex colours -- three tones on one material because splitting them would cost three draw calls per head instead of one for all four. Galvanised luma 158 is clear of the 55.5-60.5 window gatecrop erases. An earlier lift of the housing tone to luma 200 was made on a WRONG diagnosis of the gate's hole verdict and has been reverted; it moved the hole fraction by 0.0011.

A 0.56 m square plate with four proud 62 mm bolts, larger than the street columns' because this mast is 12 m and carries four heads, plus the four welded gussets that are what reads as a structural mast rather than a pipe pushed into a plate. The previous build had no baseplate at all.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Raised to hero2x with the lighting kit and heavily underspent: 540 triangles at 4 draw calls, 2 materials and 4 geometries -- 3% of the triangle ceiling. Instancing the four heads is most of the reason; so is a 12-triangle mast.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A soft key from the upper front-left; the mast's left facets read brighter than its right.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review harness parity - the harness key sits at (3, 5, 4).

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Shadow sides lifted rather than black, roughly a 0.7 shadow-to-key ratio.
No separate rim in the plate - the object separates from the backdrop by value alone.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review only; the harness rim at (0, 3, -5) is a harness convention the model must not depend on.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A near-white seamless backdrop at luma ~253; foreground coverage is 12.9%. The review harness approximates it with a HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x404040, 1.6) and NO environment map, which is why every metal here is authored below metalness 1.0: a raw metal has no diffuse term and nothing to reflect, and it renders DARKER than the 58 backdrop, which the turntable gate reads as a hole punched through the model.

The review harness applies ACES filmic tone mapping, which rolls off highlights, so a painted luma reads lower than its raw value. Albedo is therefore verified in the render and corrected against the measurement rather than copied through from the crop.

Ambient occlusion is authored per material (cavityStrength 0.2, contactShadowBias 0.3) to darken joints and seams. The prop's ground shadow is the level bake's job, not the factory's - the factory sets castShadow/receiveShadow and nothing else.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.

pivots.name: Base centre
pivots.rationale: The ONLY pivot. A floodlight mast is bolted to a foundation; the heads are aimed once at installation and are not a runtime mechanism.

animationAnchors.socketsRationale: NONE, deliberately. Nothing clips onto this prop and nothing is emitted from it; the heads are cast onto their own frame.

destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
